name: Quartz-trap archive
subtitle: data stored the way rocks record radiation

effects.effect: a crystal stores radiation as trapped charge and glows it out when heated

effect: a crystal stores radiation as trapped charge and glows it out when heated
how: Hard disks and tapes last decades, but archives need centuries. Quartz holds electrons knocked into traps by radiation for hundreds of thousands of years, which is how scientists date ancient pottery; here a fine X-ray beam traps electrons in a pattern of dots on a quartz plate, and a reader warms each dot and counts the faint glow it gives off.
obstacle: Reading a dot empties it, so each read uses up the data unless it is stored in many copies or rewritten afterwards.
why: Quartz traps really do hold charge for ages; destructive reading is the catch.
real: Electron-trapping optical memory was built in doped alkaline-earth sulfide phosphors (rewritable, UV/visible-written), and quartz TL under X-rays is studied, but nothing on X-ray-written quartz trap archival storage.
